facts.statement: Fossils of Gracilineustes have been found in Middle to Late Jurassic rock layers in England and France.
facts.quote: Fossil specimens referrable to Gracilineustes are known from Middle-Late Jurassic deposits of England and France.

facts.statement: Gracilineustes was a carnivore that spent most or all of its life in the ocean.
facts.quote: Gracilineustes was a carnivore that spent much, if not all, its life out at sea.

facts.statement: G. leedsi grew to between 2.25 and 3.11 meters long, while G. acutus reached 3.77 meters in length.
facts.quote: It was a small reptile, with G. leedsi measuring 2.25 - 3.11 m long and G. acutus measuring 3.77 m long.

facts.statement: The genus belongs to the family Metriorhynchidae and the subfamily Metriorhynchinae.
Gracilineustes lived from the Callovian to the Kimmeridgian stages, approximately 165.3 to 152.21 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Callovian to Kimmeridgian (165.3 to 152.21 million years ago)

facts.statement: Gracilineustes was a medium-sized carnivore with a tapered profile and flippers on its limbs.
facts.quote: Gracilineustes fue un carnívoro mediano, de perfil ahusado y dotado de aletas en sus extremidades

facts.statement: Fossil specimens of Gracilineustes are known from Jurassic deposits in England and France spanning the Middle to Upper periods.
facts.quote: Especímenes fósiles referibles al Gracilineustes son conocidos de depósitos jurásicos (periodos Jurásico Medio a Superior) de Inglaterra y Francia.

facts.statement: The genus Gracilineustes was described by Young and colleagues in 2010.
The type species of the genus Gracilineustes is Gracilineustes leedsi.
The authority for the genus name Gracilineustes is Young et al., 2010.
